title: Big Ten Logo Quiz: Hard Mode
headline: Can You Name The Big Ten School From A Tiny Piece Of Its Logo?
description: A hard Big Ten logo quiz: eight tiny pieces of Big Ten school logos, about 2% of each logo. Guess the school, tap to reveal the answer, keep score and share your result.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from a current Big Ten school logo, about one fiftieth of the whole mark. No full letters, no team names, no giveaways. Each piece still holds one real detail, a color pair, a curve or an edge that belongs to only one school.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

items.piece: The navy outline curving into the bottom right of the orange I.
items.fact: In its 2014 Nike refresh, Illinois kept the Block I as its primary logo and adjusted its proportions.

items.piece: The gold outline between cardinal shapes, where the S meets the C.
items.fact: USC says an interlocking SC has been in use for more than 100 years. In 2010 the Supreme Court turned away South Carolina's bid to trademark its own SC.

items.piece: The scarlet curve of the R's bowl, with its black outline.
items.fact: When Rutgers and Nike refreshed the brand in 2016, the athletic director said of the Block R: that is untouched.

items.piece: A maize corner with its navy outline, on the left side of the M.
items.fact: The Block M is Michigan's primary athletics logo, in the school's maize and blue.

items.piece: Red with gold and black outlines, inside the left leg of the M.
items.fact: Maryland's M with the state flag bar first appeared in 2013. The flag bar honors Maryland's place as the state's flagship university.

items.piece: The black shadow and red at the left edge of the W.
items.fact: Barry Alvarez picked the Motion W, drawn by Rayovac artist Rick Suchanek, as Wisconsin's helmet logo in the early 1990s.

items.piece: Purple with a thin outline, where the N's diagonal meets its left stem.
items.fact: Northwestern's trademark rules say that when an N stands alone, it must be the university's own stylized N.

items.piece: A blue curve from the bottom of the U in the script.
items.fact: UCLA simplified its script logo in 2017 and keeps it mainly for athletics.
